Infocomm Certified Technology Specialist (CTS) (Preferred)
Infocomm Certified Technology Specialist - Installation (CTS-I) (Preferred)
Experience and skill to quickly and independently troubleshoot, repair, maintain and install many different types of AV/IT equipment.

The Classroom Technology Installation Technician performs troubleshooting, maintenance, and installation of a wide variety of portable and educational technology equipment on campus in the support of teaching and learning. This position carries out systematic efforts to sustain the AV/IT infrastructure in the campus general assignment classrooms.
AV IT Engineering & Classroom Installation - 60%

Executes the installation, testing, and debugging of moderately complex AV/IT systems in classrooms and learning spaces to ensure full system commissioning. Interprets blueprints, architectural schematics, and functional diagrams to execute specialized projects, including equipment rack wiring, display device mounting, and infrastructure modifications. Collaborates with the Design and Engineering team to integrate new instructional technology subsystems into existing campus IT infrastructures. Verifies that specific phases or components of system designs are installed to plan specifications and communicates assessments (with suggested remediation, if needed) to clients.
Specialized Technical Support - 25%

Performs advanced troubleshooting and repair of analog and digital electronic components, control systems, and data transmission systems in instructional spaces. Utilizes measurement equipment to adjust and calibrate media equipment according to design specifications. Provides guidance and solutions to staff, faculty and students for the correct operation of equipment and video-data display in lecture halls and classrooms.
Process Improvement, Documentation, and Collaborative Projects - 10%

Participates as a member of cross-functional service improvement project teams to identify, evaluate, and develop complex systems and procedures. Participates in product research to identify emerging trends in hardware and software Assists in reviewing and estimating schedules and design costs, including equipment, installation, labor, and materials. Authors and maintains knowledge base documentation and staff-facing training materials to ensure consistent support and operational efficiency.
Other duties as required by the department and projects of the department - 5%
Other duties as required by the department and projects of the department
Prompt and effective communication with team members, faculty, and campus colleagues.
Self-motivated and works independently and as part of a team.
Able to learn effectively and meet deadlines.
Ability to work evenings and nights. The schedule work hour start is 5pm or later on weekdays.
Strong knowledge of AV IT installation and field implementation.
Demonstrated ability to create AV flow diagrams, schematics and AV infrastructure drawings.
Ability to test and operate installed AV IT equipment.
Knowledge of audio, video and control systems as well as architectural and cabling requirements.
Basic knowledge of electronic theory, practical system designs, analog and digital circuitry.
Demonstrates problem-solving skills.
Knowledge of PC and Mac computers and commonly used software such as Microsoft Office, AV equipment configuration software, and Google software suite.
